gaps.sentence: I don't like this colour — do you have it in ___ colours?
gaps.explanation: 'Other colours' uses 'other' as an adjective before the plural noun; 'another' is followed by singular nouns.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with rude customers.
___ the information you gave was correct.
gaps.explanation: 'All the information' is correct; 'none/neither' would need 'of' and 'both' requires two separate countable items.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was ___ attended than the organisers had hoped.
gaps.explanation: 'Well attended' compares with the adverb: less well attended.

gaps.sentence: She made very ___ mistakes in the essay, so she nearly got full marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Very few mistakes' means almost none, which explains the high mark; 'mistakes' is countable.

gaps.sentence: ___ of what he says is nonsense.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of what he says' is the pattern 'most of + noun clause'; 'the most of' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: We need to find ___ who can fix the boiler.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement: an unknown but existing person
gaps.explanation: 'Someone' is used in affirmative sentences; 'anyone' belongs to questions and negatives.
